title: The misalignment stress test
question: Does 40% more solder give you a better joint?
assumptions: Recorded native equilibria under artificial planning inputs. Physical accuracy is unqualified.
The declared fixture objective is lateral restoration without upward separating force. It is not a manufacturer requirement.
Only one isolated joint is solved. The footprint is geometric context, not a coupled board or package simulation.
The gap is held by an external fixture. It is not a prediction of free package height.
Fully wetted pinned circular rims and fixed liquid volume are assumptions. This does not predict initial wetting or whether a joint forms.
Discrete offsets are independent static equilibria. They do not predict motion, alignment time, capture range, bridges or yield.
Mesh topology and refinement checks do not prove a unique global equilibrium or certify self-intersection absence.
The existing physical force-validation failure remains unresolved. These cases do not qualify the example alloy or process.
baseline: Published Eq. 9 is a strong simple alternative for aligned lightly loaded height. It does not answer this nonzero-offset, fixed-gap lateral and axial force question. Surface Evolver itself already supplies the numerical capability. This demo adds inspectable PCB context and a reproducible comparison.
